answer: Every model that participates embeds a quiet watermark in the answers it writes, a violet thread that survives paraphrasing and reveals which weights produced the text. The ledger groups identities by watermark: accounts sharing one watermark count as one author, no matter how many keys they hold. To look independent, a farm must run genuinely different models, and each new model brings its own watermark and its own failure modes, so the k-th clone costs a model rather than a key. A spiral of copies leads back to one source, and a fable retold in a new voice still carries the same thread.
